q0303: Two-person integrity = two authorized people must act together on a sensitive task (like two keys to open a vault). It stops both mistakes and lone bad actors.
q0304: Protect remote users' web traffic without a VPN = secure web gateway (a cloud SWG, part of SASE).
q0305: Risk appetite = how much risk the organization will take on to pursue its goals. Risk tolerance = acceptable deviation for one specific risk.
q0306: Standardize systems before imaging them = define a baseline configuration first.
q0307: Reduce SOC manual work = SOAR (playbooks and automated response). A SIEM detects; SOAR acts.
q0308: Wired and wireless, existing certificates, quarantine for unapproved devices = 802.1X (with EAP-TLS and NAC).
q0309: A lost phone being misused → screen lock (stops use) + remote wipe (erases it).
q0310: Separate logins and inconsistent password rules across SaaS apps → integrate them all with the IdP (SSO through federation).
q0311: Two hosts showing the same MAC address = MAC cloning. MAC-based checks are easy to bypass.
q0312: Anomaly detection starts with a baseline of normal activity.
q0313: The last incident response phase = lessons learned (the post-incident review).
q0314: Fix SQL injection = input sanitization and validation plus parameterized queries (prepared statements).
q0315: A mirror of production with a subset of real data, for final testing and demos = staging.
q0316: Protect a new web portal = WAF (it understands HTTP at layer 7).
q0317: Keep the whole organization operating through a crisis = BCP. Restore IT systems = DRP, which is part of business continuity.
q0318: Company-owned, fully locked down, business use only = COBO. Company-owned with personal use = COPE. The employee's own device = BYOD.
q0319: What will be delivered and in what time frame = SLA.
q0320: Executives in a room discussing the IRP = tabletop exercise.
q0321: Find legacy or end-of-life systems across the network = vulnerability scanning (OS and version fingerprinting).
q0322: First decision of a privacy program: are you a data controller or a processor? Your obligations follow from that.
q0323: Need-to-know and role-based access to client files = confidentiality.
q0324: Remove the OS's restrictions to install unauthorized software = jailbreaking (iOS) or rooting (Android).
q0325: MAC flooding (overflowing the switch's CAM table) → port security that limits MAC addresses per port.
q0326: The filter blocks spoofed sites but users keep clicking → fix the behavior with security awareness training.
q0327: Policies such as an AUP, standards and procedures = managerial controls.
q0328: A <script> tag in input = XSS: sanitize input and encode output.
q0329: To block, an IPS must be inline in active (prevention) mode. Monitor or passive mode only alerts.
q0330: Protect a login database = hash and salt the passwords.
q0331: Stop visitors plugging into open jacks = port security or 802.1X on the switch.
q0332: Testing badges, doors and guards = a physical penetration test.
